overview: This Senate resolution directs the Architect of the Capitol, the office that maintains the Capitol building, to display a plaque honoring the police and other law enforcement officers who defended the Capitol on January 6, 2021. A 2022 spending law required such a plaque to be placed on the west front of the Capitol. Under this resolution, the plaque would be shown in a publicly accessible spot in the Senate wing until it can be installed in that permanent location. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on January 8, 2026.
for: Supporters say the officers who protected Congress that day deserve public recognition, and the plaque required by law should be displayed rather than kept out of view.
against: Critics say the resolution is a temporary display decision that does not resolve when the plaque will be installed in its permanent place as the law requires.
